task: find and change an app's settings inside the Shopify admin

sources.title: Polaris pattern: App settings layout (default variant, source)
sources.note: Shopify/polaris was archived on 2026-09-11; the pattern text last changed 2023-12-11. The 'How it helps merchants' section states the reasons.

sources.title: Shopify app home: Settings template
sources.note: Current guidance: section heading + subheading per group, nested sections for items with status, Save Bar, Modal confirmation, Toast.

sources.title: Shopify app design guidelines: Layout
sources.note: Settings layout = narrower left column (title, description) + wider right column (form). 4px grid. Do not change density within a page. At most one primary action per card.

sources.title: design-extract (designlang 13.4.0) run on the settings template page
sources.note: Measures the shopify.dev documentation site, not the Shopify admin. Pattern spacing comes from the pattern code (Polaris space tokens), not from this run.

decisions.statement: A settings page is a vertical stack of groups; each group is two columns: a narrower left column with the group title and a short description, and a wider right column with that group's inputs inside a card.
decisions.why: Stated by the pattern: left-column labels and descriptions let merchants scan the page and find what they need; right-column cards make a setting easy to configure once found, or to configure several related settings together.
decisions.counterexample: One or two settings in total: a single card. Narrow viewports: the pattern itself collapses to one column.

decisions.statement: Setting groups stack vertically, separated by a divider from the small breakpoint up; they are never placed side by side.
decisions.why: Stated usage guidance ('stack all setting groups vertically'); preserves top-to-bottom scanning.
decisions.counterexample: When the task is comparison (plan A vs plan B), that is a comparison table, not a settings page.

decisions.statement: A group description is written only when it helps; a body paragraph is never used in place of the group heading's subheading.
decisions.why: Stated usage guidance ('don't include a description unless it's helpful'; 'don't use a body paragraph as the group description').
decisions.counterexample: Settings whose effect is invisible on the page (tax rules, retention periods) need a description.

decisions.statement: From the medium breakpoint the two columns are 2fr : 5fr with a 16px gap; groups are 16px apart from the small breakpoint and 32px apart below it; below medium the layout is one column.
decisions.why: Values read from the pattern's live-preview code: InlineGrid columns {xs: '1fr', md: '2fr 5fr'} gap='400', BlockStack gap {xs: '800', sm: '400'}; Polaris space-400 = 16px, space-800 = 32px.
decisions.counterexample: On very wide screens the input column would grow too wide; the current template keeps the page at inlineSize='small' instead of scaling the ratio.

decisions.statement: Saving is a save bar that appears only when there are unsaved changes; destructive actions such as 'reset all settings' open a confirmation modal; a toast reports the result.
decisions.why: Stated by the template: grouping options and protecting unsaved changes keeps the page usable; Save Bar, Modal and Toast APIs are the prescribed mechanisms.
decisions.counterexample: A single immediate toggle (notifications on/off) saves inline; the template does not cover inline save, so that remains unknown for this source.

decisions.statement: Items that carry their own status or action (connected accounts, tools) are nested sections, so each item's heading, status badge and action sit together in its header.
decisions.why: Stated by the template's nested-section guidance.
decisions.counterexample: A group of plain inputs with no per-item status is one card.

decisions.statement: Spacing follows a 4px grid; density does not change within one page; an interactive card has at most one primary action; paragraphs are not placed directly on the page background.
decisions.why: Stated in the layout guidelines ('avoid changing information density within a single page, otherwise your app can feel disjointed'; 'avoid placing paragraphs of text directly on the background').
decisions.counterexample: A data table region may be tighter than the form, but on the same 4px multiples.

ruleCandidates.statement: A settings screen is a vertical stack of groups, each laid out as [title + optional description | input card] in two columns; the left column is for scanning, the right for editing.
ruleCandidates.applicability: pageType settings; grammars operations-console and consumer-service; viewports from about 768px.
ruleCandidates.allowedVariation: Column ratio between 1:2 and 2:5; description omitted; divider optional; page width capped rather than ratio scaled.
ruleCandidates.counterexample: Three or fewer settings: one card. Narrow viewports: one column. First-run setup wizards: sequential-story, not this layout. Products that use a left navigation plus a single column (GitHub settings) are a different, equally valid system; this rule does not override an approved project system.
ruleCandidates.verification: ss-verify measures column count and ratio per group at 1440 and 390; ss-score Layout deducts for groups placed side by side or inputs without a group heading.

ruleCandidates.statement: A settings group heading is a title plus at most one short subheading; a body paragraph is not used as the description.
ruleCandidates.counterexample: Settings with invisible effects need a description; it is still one or two sentences in the subheading role.
ruleCandidates.verification: Check text length under each group heading (more than two sentences flags); reviewer confirms the description adds information.

ruleCandidates.statement: A multi-field settings form uses a save bar that appears only with unsaved changes, confirms destructive actions in a dialog, and reports the result with a toast.
ruleCandidates.applicability: settings forms that save several fields together.
ruleCandidates.allowedVariation: Immediate toggles save inline and report with a toast; the bar may be fixed to the bottom or the top.
ruleCandidates.counterexample: Single-field settings; platforms where autosave is the convention (mobile OS settings).
ruleCandidates.verification: ss-verify functional scenario: change a field → bar appears → save → toast; leave with unsaved changes → confirmation.

ruleCandidates.statement: A list of items with their own status (connections, tools) gives each item a header row with title, status badge and action; a card carries at most one primary action.
ruleCandidates.applicability: settings lists of integrations, accounts, devices.
ruleCandidates.allowedVariation: Actions collapse into a single menu when more than two.
ruleCandidates.counterexample: Plain input groups with no per-item status.
ruleCandidates.verification: Each item header contains a status element and an action; count of primary buttons per card ≤ 1 (ss-score States and Navigation).

ruleCandidates.statement: One spacing system per settings page, on 4px multiples; density does not change between groups.
ruleCandidates.allowedVariation: A table region may use tighter steps of the same scale.
ruleCandidates.counterexample: None found; this is close to a floor rule and already matches VISUAL-CRAFT CR-1.
ruleCandidates.verification: ss-verify spacing-role measurement reports one scale and no role drift between groups.
